title: Hybrid tensor-layout-aware kernel hedging & autotuner for mixed prefill/decode workloads
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Build and ship a lightweight, online kernel hedging/autotuning layer that (1) reasons about tensor layout and memory-stride characteristics, (2) combines short microbench probes with a small Bayesian updater to pick kernels per-arch and per-seqlen bucket, and (3) integrates token-phase awareness so prefill-heavy and decode-heavy flows get different default strategies.

Background: We have many kernels (flash-attn variants, fused qkv, tiled matmul implementations) that perform differently depending on sequence-length distribution, head-dim, batch mix (prefill vs decode), and physical tensor layout produced by preceding ops (transposed vs contiguous). Historically we choose kernels by static heuristics or expensive offline benchmarks. This ticket proposes an online, low-cost hedging/autotuner that minimizes regret while keeping tail latency and SLOs intact.

Why different from current work: Existing autotuners focus on seqlen/arch profiling or large microbenchmark suites. This approach explicitly models tensor memory stride and token-phase (prefill vs decode) and uses an exploration schedule that is safe for tail latency (hedged probes during warm windows and lightweight continuous sampling during idle cycles). It also produces per-customer lightweight profiles that survive restarts and are shared as anonymized seed tables across a region cluster.
proposed_solution: 1) Build a probe runner in the runtime that can execute ~10-50 short kernel microcalls (10-50ms total) in a background low-priority worker. 2) Extract features: arch signature (GPU model), free memory, tensor stride/contiguity flags from upstream ops, head_dim, kv-cache usage, sequence-length bucket, and token-phase. 3) Maintain a small Bayesian belief over kernel performance per (arch, seqlen-bucket, tensor-layout, token-phase). 4) Choose default kernel from belief mean; occasionally (epsilon-decay) run microprobes to update beliefs. 5) Safety: enforce a latency safety margin -- never switch to a kernel with predicted P95 > current kernel P95 * 1.15 without a gradual canary window. 6) Instrumentation: record probe results and decisions to the console, expose a per-route kernel-score chart and drift alerts. 7) Add a "tensor-layout priority" preselector that biases kernel set depending on whether tensors are stored row-major, channel-first, or with strided transpositions. 8) Provide an API toggle for Dedicated/Private to opt into region-wide shared seed tables or opt-out for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Autotuner can complete a warm microprobe cycle (<50ms) without increasing P99 for production routes by more than 5% under typical load
End-to-end integration shows median token throughput improvement >= 6% on mixed prefill/decode workloads for at least two open-source models (Llama2-13B and Mistral-7B) on A100 and H100 instances
Runtime emits kernel decision events and a per-route kernel-score metric to Console; charts populated in runtime-2.1 staging dashboard
Canary rollout infrastructure can rollback kernel switches automatically if P95 regressions exceed the safety bound for two consecutive minutes
Security review sign-off for optional seed sharing in Dedicated/Private environments
experiment_plan: Stage 0 (lab): Implement probe harness and offline microbench collection across target hardware and tensor-layout permutations (1 week)
Stage 1 (staging): Enable hedging/autotune in staging for a small set of routes with synthetic prefill/decode mixes; collect baseline and tuned metrics (2 weeks)
Stage 2 (canary): Enable on 5% of production traffic for low-risk customers; monitor latency regressions, GPU utilization, and kernel-switch churn (1 week)
Stage 3 (ramp): Increase canary to 30% while running continuous drift detection and seed-table aggregation (2 weeks)
Benchmarks: compare against static heuristic baseline, existing autotuner baselines using the same workload generator
rollout_plan: Feature gate behind runtime.config.enableTensorLayoutAutotune (off by default)
Start with models flagged in model-catalog as 'probe-friendly' (small-medium memory footprint)
Automated canary rollouts with 5/30/100% steps and automatic rollback on safety triggers
Ops runbook for investigating kernel-switch incidents and manually pinning routes to legacy heuristics
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Probe overhead increases tail latency —> Mitigation: limit probes to background low-priority lanes, measure per-route overhead, and bail out if overhead > 2%
Risk: Noisy probes produce oscillation —> Mitigation: exponential smoothing on beliefs and minimum dwell-time between kernel switches (default 15 min)
Risk: Seed sharing could leak capacity patterns —> Mitigation: only share hashed anonymized fingerprints and allow Dedicated customers to opt-out
Risk: Unexpected tensor-layout observation errors —> Mitigation: conservative default to current kernel unless layout flag confidence >= 0.8
instrumentation_and_metrics: Per-decision telemetry: chosen_kernel, candidate_kernels, probe_durations_ms, probe_outcome_latency_ms
Aggregates: kernel_p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_sec, GPU_utilization, memory_peak_bytes by (arch, seqlen_bucket, tensor_layout, token_phase)
Drift alerts: when empirical kernel P95 deviates >12% from belief for 1 hour
Console charts: per-route kernel-score heatmap, per-arch seed-table snapshot download
test_plan: Unit tests for belief updater and probe harness (deterministic pseudo-random probes)
Integration tests: simulate mixed prefill/decode stream and assert no more than 5% latency regression when autotune is enabled
A/B performance tests comparing tuned vs static heuristic on nightly cluster scale runner
Chaos tests: inject transient slow kernels to validate canary rollback behavior
